messages.content: I need to start planning Seattle for the university-press meetings in mid-June. The program runs Monday, June 15 through Wednesday, June 17. Can you first tell me whether I need to fly from Denver on Sunday and what a reasonable return window would be Wednesday?

Yes. What time does the first Monday appointment begin, when does the Wednesday meeting finish, and where in Seattle are the meetings being held? Those details will determine whether a very early Monday flight is viable and how much time you need to reach SEA on Wednesday.

The first appointment is at 8:30 Monday morning. Most sessions are at the Westin Seattle, and Wednesday ends at 3:30. There is also an author event at Elliott Bay Book Company Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. My office will pay for Sunday night if necessary.

A Sunday arrival is the practical choice. The earliest Monday nonstop from Denver would leave almost no recovery margin before an 8:30 appointment, even if it operated on time. For Wednesday, I would target departures no earlier than about 6:30 p.m. The Westin to SEA typically takes roughly 40 minutes by Link light rail or 30-50 minutes by car, and you should allow extra time after the 3:30 finish to collect luggage.
That makes sense. Please look at Sunday afternoon or early evening nonstops and Wednesday flights after 6:30. Economy is fine. I am traveling alone.

I found three useful round trips in the current schedule. Alaska departs Denver Sunday at 3:10 p.m. and reaches Seattle at 5:15 p.m.; its Wednesday return leaves at 7:25 p.m. and arrives in Denver at 11:03 p.m., priced around $287. United leaves Sunday at 1:35 p.m., arrives at 3:38 p.m., and returns Wednesday at 8:15 p.m., reaching Denver at 11:51 p.m., around $305. Delta leaves Sunday at 6:05 p.m., arrives at 8:10 p.m., and returns Wednesday at 6:40 p.m., arriving in Denver at 10:14 p.m., around $329. All are nonstop economy fares before any optional extras.
Is the 6:40 Delta return genuinely workable, or would I be rushing out of the last meeting?

It is workable but tight. If the meeting ends promptly at 3:30 and your bag is ready at the hotel, you could leave downtown around 3:50 and normally reach SEA with adequate time. A meeting overrun, heavy road traffic, or a slow luggage stop would reduce the cushion. The 7:25 Alaska flight provides a more comfortable margin, while the 8:15 United flight is the least pressured.
Keep all three for the moment. Now help me understand the hotel geography. Is Elliott Bay far enough from the Westin that I should consider staying closer to the bookstore?

Elliott Bay Book Company is in Capitol Hill, about 1.5 miles from the Westin. For Tuesday evening, expect roughly 10-20 minutes by car depending on traffic. Transit is also manageable: walk to Westlake Station, take Link one stop to Capitol Hill, then walk several blocks to the bookstore. Staying downtown makes the three meeting days simplest; staying in Capitol Hill improves Tuesday evening but adds a commute on Monday, Tuesday morning, and Wednesday.
Please compare the Westin itself, one less expensive downtown option, and one credible Capitol Hill option. I need three nights, Sunday through Wednesday.

The Westin is about $1,041 including estimated taxes for June 14-17, with the advantage of being in the meeting building. The Hyatt Regency Seattle is roughly $918 including taxes; it is about a 10-minute walk from the Westin. The Silver Cloud Hotel Seattle-Broadway in Capitol Hill is about $804 including taxes, approximately a 7-minute ride or 15-minute walk from Elliott Bay, but morning travel to the Westin can take 15-25 minutes by transit or car. These are current comparison totals and can change until booked.
Does the Hyatt create any difficulty Wednesday if I leave my suitcase there during the meetings?

No significant difficulty. You could check out Wednesday morning, leave the suitcase with the Hyatt, attend the sessions at the Westin, and walk back after the 3:30 finish. Allow about 20-25 minutes to return to the Hyatt, retrieve the bag, and get moving toward the airport. That makes the 6:40 flight less attractive, but the 7:25 and 8:15 departures remain reasonable.
And if I stay at the Westin, I can retrieve it immediately after the meeting, correct?

Correct. You could check the bag with the Westin Wednesday morning and collect it as soon as the final session ends. Assuming a 3:45 departure from the hotel, the 6:40 Delta flight would have a usable cushion, though the later flights would still be more forgiving.

Build three complete combinations rather than mixing every flight with every hotel. I want one centered on convenience, one that costs less without making the meetings awkward, and one that makes the Tuesday event easier.

Convenience combination: Alaska nonstop, Sunday 3:10-5:15 p.m. and Wednesday 7:25-11:03 p.m., plus three nights at the Westin. Estimated total is $1,328. You arrive with time for dinner Sunday, stay at the meeting site, and have nearly four hours between the scheduled Wednesday finish and departure.

Lower-cost downtown combination: United nonstop, Sunday 1:35-3:38 p.m. and Wednesday 8:15-11:51 p.m., plus the Hyatt Regency. Estimated total is $1,223. The hotel is a short walk from the meetings, and the later return leaves ample time to retrieve luggage.

Tuesday-event combination: Delta nonstop, Sunday 6:05-8:10 p.m. and Wednesday 6:40-10:14 p.m., plus the Silver Cloud Broadway. Estimated total is $1,133. It is convenient for Elliott Bay, but it creates three cross-neighborhood meeting commutes and the tightest Wednesday airport transfer.
The third one is cheaper, but pairing Capitol Hill with the earliest return seems like the wrong combination. Can you substitute a later flight there?

Yes. Pairing the Silver Cloud with the United flights is more coherent: Sunday 1:35-3:38 p.m., Wednesday 8:15-11:51 p.m., and three hotel nights for an estimated $1,109 total. You would have enough time Wednesday to return to Capitol Hill, collect your bag, and reach SEA without relying on a perfect meeting finish.
Good. Between the Westin package and the Hyatt package, what am I really buying for the extra $105 at the Westin?

Primarily time and simplicity. At the Westin, the meetings, room, and luggage storage are in one building, so there is no morning walk and no hotel detour Wednesday afternoon. The Hyatt saves about $105 and remains close enough that the commute is modest, but you would walk roughly 10 minutes each way and spend part of Wednesday's airport cushion retrieving your bag there. The flight differences also matter: the Alaska package gets you home 48 minutes earlier than the United package.
I think the Hyatt and United combination is the sensible middle option. Before I settle on it, lay out the Sunday arrival, Tuesday evening movement, and Wednesday departure in practical terms.

Sunday: leave Denver at 1:35 p.m., arrive at SEA at 3:38 p.m., and expect to reach the Hyatt around 5:00 p.m. by Link plus a walk, or somewhat earlier by car if traffic is light.

Tuesday: after the meetings at the Westin, walk to Westlake Station and take Link to Capitol Hill for the 7:00 p.m. Elliott Bay event. The bookstore is several blocks from the station. Afterward, return by Link or take a short car ride to the Hyatt.

Wednesday: check out and leave your bag with the Hyatt, attend the final sessions at the Westin, then walk back after the 3:30 finish. A departure from the hotel by about 4:15-4:30 gives substantial room for the trip to SEA and the 8:15 p.m. United flight. Arrival in Denver is scheduled for 11:51 p.m.
Please keep that as the leading plan, with Alaska plus the Westin as the convenience alternative. Do not book anything yet. Give me the two totals and note what still needs verification.

Leading plan: United nonstop flights plus the Hyatt Regency Seattle for June 14-17, estimated at $1,223 total. The outbound is Sunday at 1:35 p.m., arriving at 3:38 p.m.; the return is Wednesday at 8:15 p.m., arriving in Denver at 11:51 p.m.

Convenience alternative: Alaska nonstop flights plus the Westin Seattle for the same dates, estimated at $1,328 total. The outbound is Sunday at 3:10 p.m., arriving at 5:15 p.m.; the return is Wednesday at 7:25 p.m., arriving in Denver at 11:03 p.m.

Before booking, the live fare and room totals, fare restrictions, hotel cancellation deadlines, and final flight schedules need to be rechecked. Nothing has been reserved or changed on your other trips.
